title: Root logging profile changes can be skipped after any handler is installed
reasoning: configure_logging computes the intended root level from the selected profile or LOG_LEVEL, but applies it only through logging.basicConfig. In Python, basicConfig is a no-op once the root logger already has handlers, which is common when a server, test harness, or embedding host initializes logging first. In that case the profile-specific root level and format are silently not applied, while the function still proceeds to mutate selected named loggers, leaving logging in a partially configured state. The included tests cover constants and the LiteLLM helper, but they do not exercise configure_logging with a pre-existing root handler, so this regression would pass.
reproduction: Install any root handler before calling configure_logging, then call configure_logging(profile="verbose") and observe that the root logger level/format is not changed by logging.basicConfig.
recommendation: Make configure_logging explicitly set the root logger level and either pass force=True to basicConfig where acceptable or update existing handlers intentionally. If preserving existing handlers is required, document that behavior and set only the root level directly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests import _IMPORTANT_PROFILE_LOGGERS and _configure_litellm_runtime_flags only; they never call configure_logging or simulate an already-configured root logger.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that attaches a temporary root handler, calls configure_logging(profile="verbose") with LOG_LEVEL unset, and asserts the root logger is set to DEBUG or that the intended handler policy is applied deterministically.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/core/logging_setup.py plus focused tests in tests/backend/test_logging_setup.py
